claims.text: An ML interatomic potential trained on diverse ab initio solid and liquid configurations will represent near-equiatomic HEA configurational diversity more faithfully than traditional EAM references.
The ML reference will improve reference–target phase-space overlap in thermodynamic integration.
The target materials are multicomponent, near-equiatomic HEAs typically containing refractory or high-melting elements.
The target HEAs are sampled in both solid and liquid states near their melting temperatures.
The ML potential should be trained on extensive ab initio data from both solid and liquid configurations.
The method is applicable within approximately 50–100 K above or below the melting temperature.
The ML potential can continuously map the diverse local atomic environments found in the high-temperature solid and liquid.
The ML potential captures liquid disorder and high-temperature anharmonic effects.
Incorporating a broad spectrum of ab initio configurations from both phases enhances statistical overlap between the reference ensemble and the target ab initio system.
Improved statistical overlap produces a smoother thermodynamic-integration path.
A smoother thermodynamic-integration path reduces reference–target free-energy mismatch.
The ML reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately 20–30% relative to TOR-TILD EAM references.
The proposed intervention will produce more consistent free-energy estimates.
Traditional EAM potentials used in TOR-TILD cannot capture the full configurational diversity of ab initio HEA liquids.
The intervention will be most effective for near-equiatomic HEAs near melting.
The benefits will be less pronounced in alloys with strong local ordering, severe compositional inhomogeneity, or temperatures far from melting.
The anticipated 20–30% mismatch reduction is based on analogous elemental and binary calculations.
The quantitative improvement may vary across different HEA chemistries.
